checks.detail: p=9,q=1,m=n gives n!^9/(n!)^2=n!^7. The first finite product t-1,...,t-n equals the rising Pochhammer (t-n)_n by reordering; the second is (t+n+1)_n. The pole product is exactly product(k=0..n,t+k)^9.

checks.check: coefficient defined from genuine rational product
checks.detail: actualR is numerator/poleProduct^9; clearedR removes exactly the j factor; leadingPoleCoefficient is clearedR evaluated at -j. Its definition contains no closed binomial coefficient formula.

clear_highest_pole assumes j<=n and every t+k !=0, then proves actualR*(t+j)^9=clearedR. The proof factors the pole product and supplies nonzero factor and deleted product. clearedPoleProduct_ne_zero proves the denominator at -j is nonzero, even without j<=n.

checks.check: actual product computation of highest coefficient
checks.detail: numerator_eval derives (-1)^n*n!^9*choose(n+j,n)*choose(2n-j,n). clearedPoleProduct_eval derives (-1)^j*j!*(n-j)!. Their ninth-power quotient, factorial nonzero facts and Nat.cast_choose give the formula; it is not a definitional rfl substitution.
The specialized phase (-1)^(9j+n) equals (-1)^(n+j). Factors are choose(n,j)^9, choose(n+j,n), choose(2n-j,n). The general theorem covers odd n; only the even corollary drops (-1)^n.

Independent Lean wrappers prove leadingPoleCoefficient(0,0)=1, (1,0)=-2, (1,1)=2, and (2,1)=-4608. n=0 uses empty numerator/deleted products. At a pole totalized rational division in actualR is not substituted into the clearing identity, whose regularity hypothesis is explicit.

For every j<=n all three binomial factors are strictly positive, so the actual coefficient is nonzero. Its explicit integer witness is the signed binomial product. The final rfl in the integer proof checks casts after leadingPoleCoefficient_eq has already been proved.
For even n, (-1)^j*leadingPoleCoefficient(n,j)>0 follows by squaring the sign and positivity of all three actual binomial factors. No replacement positive coefficient is introduced.

checks.check: actual weighted family and local coordinate
checks.detail: weightedR is actualR times W.eval(t*(t+n)); the coordinate t=-j+z is exactly -j(n-j)+(n-2j)z+z^2, with no n^-2 scaling. The weighted regular-point clearing theorem follows from the actual unweighted identity.

For every W in Q[X], the highest cleared value is the actual unweighted coefficient multiplied by W(-j(n-j)). This formalizes the highest-order term of Eq(5) and the exact local coordinate identity, not the whole lower-order Taylor convolution.

The independent Lean audit proves weightedLeadingPoleCoefficient !=0 iff W(-j(n-j)) !=0, using the actual unweighted nonzero theorem. It also proves W=X+1 cancels the highest coefficient at n=2,j=1. A nonzero polynomial W therefore does not by itself give a nonzero highest coefficient.
